# Two deepest witnesses: actual max sharing and critical-menu dependence

This exact calibration was proposed by root and independently checked
here. It contains two distinct deepest source fibers, two actual ordered
propagations, strictly cheaper pointwise-max sharing, and complete
all-normal global depth formulas. It also shows that one genuinely
critical menu pays while another genuinely critical menu fails on the
SAME deformation. No parity bound or universal paying selection is inferred.

## 1. Why taking a maximum changes an actual deformation

Suppose finitely many convex-fiber families on one fixed complete integer
base are compatible: every anchored convex combination of input fibers
is contained in the target fiber. Their pointwise intersections are also
compatible. Indeed any convex combination of intersected inputs belongs
to each original combination and hence to each original target.

In particular, if two erosion families use inequalities

    n.x+e V_z^(r)(n,x)<=h_(K_z)(n),   r=1,2,

then their fiberwise intersection is EXACTLY the erosion with field
max(V_z^(1),V_z^(2)). A maximum of continuous nonnegative convex-in-x
fields has the same properties. The established continuum-normal
variation formula therefore gives

    D_max=sum_z integral_(boundary K_z) max(V_z^(1),V_z^(2)) dS
          <= D_1+D_2.                                      (1)

The difference is the integral of the smaller speed and is strictly
positive when the two speeds overlap on positive boundary measure.
This is a change in actual boundary velocity and original-mass cost,
not a coupling optimization with fixed source marginals. Cap losses
must also be recomputed using that same maximum field. In arbitrary
families this observation does not assert that the SUM field itself
defines a compatible family; in the example below it explicitly does.

## 2. Actual four-fiber data and both deepest witnesses

Take n=d=1 and

    C=[-1,2] x [-1,1],
    P={-1,0,1,2}, K_z=[-1,1].                              (2)

The total mixed measure is M=8. Both (0,0) and (1,0) have raw depth3.
For the first point, reflection of the fiber at -1 onto the fiber at1
shows that every closed containing ambient halfspace captures total
endpoint length at least2. Its middle-fiber contribution is at least1.
The fourth fiber contributes nonnegative mass. This proves the lower
bound3 for ALL ambient orientations, including pure integer normals and
closed halfspaces carrying whole-fiber boundary mass. The second source
has the symmetric proof.

The two pairs of actual critical caps

    H0^+:  x-z>=0,      H0^-: -x-z>=0,
    H1^+:  x+(z-1)>=0,  H1^-: -x+(z-1)>=0                (3)

each have raw mass3 and cover their assigned source plane. The endpoint
fibers have maximum raw depth1: an ambient integer tilt isolates any
ordinary half-interval, while the own interval provides the reverse
bound. Thus their cap covers have strict slack below3. These facts prove
the exact GLOBAL normalized maximum beta=3/8 and identify two actual
deepest witness sources, not merely two selected candidates.

## 3. Forward, reverse, maximum, and sum fields

At each source in(2), the ordinary centroid projective field is the
constant support distance1 for both normals. Start with that own demand
at bases0 and1 and order the base increasingly. The extreme nontrivial
anchored representations are

    0=(1/2)(-1)+(1/2)1=(2/3)(-1)+(1/3)2,
    1=(1/3)(-1)+(2/3)2=(1/2)0+(1/2)2.                   (4)

Pay each target demand using its higher input. Its coefficient lambda
requires input field target/lambda. Taking a maximum whenever demands
meet gives, in base order(-1,0,1,2),

    g_forward=(0,1,2,4).                                 (5)

Explicitly g1=max(1,2g0)=2 and
g2=max(3g0,(3/2)g1,2g1)=4. The decreasing order gives the reflected
actual propagation

    g_reverse=(4,2,1,0).

Their pointwise maximum and sum are

    g_max=(4,2,2,4),   g_sum=(4,3,3,4).                  (6)

All four vectors are convex sequences. For any such vector g and
0<e<1/4, define the fiber radii 1-e*g_z and interpolate those radii
linearly between consecutive bases. This interpolation is concave, so
the region |x|<=r(z), -1<=z<=2 is a full-dimensional convex body whose
complete four integer fibers are exactly the intended intervals.
Thus every family just displayed is an ACTUAL compatible deformation.

The maximum INTEGER FIBERS are the intersections of the forward and
reverse fibers. The chosen linearly interpolated fiber hull may be
smaller than their full ambient-body intersection at noninteger bases;
their mixed sets and measures are exactly the same. Its exact first
total cost is24, whereas the sum family's is28:

    M_max(e)=8-24e,       M_sum(e)=8-28e.                 (7)

The strict saving4 is actual removed length saved on the two source
fibers, where the incoming demands overlap. At the other bases the
maximum also represents the shared incoming constraints in(4), not
independent copies of removed boundary mass.

## 4. Complete global depths and a strict improvement from sharing

In the maximum family the outer radius is R=1-4e and the inner radius
is r=1-2e. In the sum family they are R=1-4e and r=1-3e. In both cases
0<R<=r. Reflection of the smaller outer interval into the opposite
inner interval gives raw depth at least r+2R at either source center,
for every closed ambient containing halfspace. The caps(3) have exactly
this mass: one outer interval is full, the source contributes its half,
and the opposite inner and remaining outer intervals are empty.
Those same caps cover the complete source planes. The endpoint maxima
are R<r+2R. Consequently the exact global raw maxima are

    Q_max(e)=3-10e,      Q_sum(e)=3-11e.                  (8)

For every 0<e<1/4,

    (3-10e)/(8-24e) < (3-11e)/(8-28e) < 3/8.             (9)

The comparison numerator for the first inequality is
-4e(1-4e)<0. The respective derivatives at zero are -1/8 and -1/16.
Thus max sharing strictly improves actual global normalized descent,
not just a denominator estimate with unproved criticality.

For each fixed cap in(3), the maximum path loses10 to first order and
the sum path loses11. Their first-order normalized payments are

    10-(3/8)24=1,
    11-(3/8)28=1/2.                                     (10)

The supporting statuses matter. For H0^+ the original base -1 is wholly
captured with an inside supporting contact; base0 is cut at its center;
base1 has only its outside supporting endpoint captured; base2 is empty.
The corresponding maximum-path losses are8,2,0,0. Counting the closed
outside endpoint as positive captured volume loss would be wrong.
The other caps are symmetric.

## 5. A different genuine critical menu fails on the same path

Replace the integer slopes in(3) by1/2:

    J0^+: x-z/2>=0,      J0^-: -x-z/2>=0,
    J1^+: x+(z-1)/2>=0,  J1^-: -x+(z-1)/2>=0.           (11)

At e=0 these are also actual critical caps of mass3, and their pairs
cover exactly the same source planes. On the maximum path, for
0<e<1/8, each has mass

    3-8e.                                                (12)

For example J0^+ receives proper positive pieces in bases -1,0,1,
with losses4,2,2, and has an outside supporting contact of zero loss
at base2. Its payment is8-(3/8)24=-1. This selected fixed cover therefore
fails to certify descent, even though the actual depth decreases by(8).

This is a precise bounded selection obstruction: max sharing changes
real costs, but it does not make every original critical profile pay.
Choosing the genuinely critical menu(3) instead of(11) is essential in
this example. No inference that such a paying choice always exists at a
bad minimum is made.

The sign difference is visible in the EXACT shared-field correction.
Here min(g_forward,g_reverse)=(0,1,1,0), with total cost4. A cap in(3)
has shared loss1, hence shared surplus1-(3/8)4=-1/2; subtracting that
shared field improves payment from1/2 to1. A cap in(11) instead has
shared loss2 and shared surplus+1/2; its sum-field payment is-1/2,
and removing the overlap worsens it to-1. The minimum field itself is
not asserted to define a compatible family. This is an identity of
physical first costs and losses, explaining why cost sharing and cap
selection cannot be optimized independently even in this actual example.

The verifier `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_two_witness_max_sharing_interval_defect_transport.py`
checks every finite original/perturbed cap measure and the exact global
comparison identities. The all-direction lower bounds are the reflection
proof above, not numerical sampling.

## 6. Merging two actual descent paths can erase all descent

There is a separate exact three-fiber obstruction to promoting the max
closure to preservation of payment. Start with the three equal intervals
at bases -1,0,1. The unique deepest fiber is the middle, with raw maximum3,
total6 and normalized depth1/2. One-source upward propagation gives

    g_forward=(0,1,2), g_reverse=(2,1,0),
    g_max=(2,1,2).                                        (14)

All three sequences are convex, hence give actual compatible interval
families. For 0<e<1/4, each individual path has middle radius1-e and
endpoint radii1 and1-2e in opposite order. Reflection of the smaller
endpoint interval into the larger one gives the lower bound3-5e at the
middle center. A sufficiently steep integer tilt captures just the
smaller endpoint and an ordinary half of the middle, attaining it.
Such two opposite-continuous-normal caps cover the middle plane; the
endpoint raw maxima are at most1<3-5e. Therefore BOTH individual paths
have exact global normalized depth

    beta_individual(e)=(3-5e)/(6-6e)<1/2.                (15)

Their derivative at zero is-1/3. But the maximum path has equal endpoint
radii1-2e, so the same reflection and upper-cap argument gives raw
maximum3-5e and total6-10e. Thus

    beta_max(e)=(3-5e)/(6-10e)=1/2                       (16)

IDENTICALLY. This is not just a failure of a chosen first-order cover:
the actual global maximum is unchanged. The two individually paying
menus isolate opposite endpoints; max compatibility does not make
their signed payments consistent. These data do not contradict any
above-target OC guarantee. They exclude an unconditional rule that the
pointwise maximum of actual descending propagation arrays must itself
descend, even for a single genuine deepest witness and complete bases.
